AMD does not fit the WFE/process-step axes, so it is left unranked rather than ranked on price
The holdings sizes conflict across state (AMAT and TER flagged as dust, but the ladder shows $1.3k and $1.8k), so the row may be stale
The prior ladder's leader, TER, underperformed within the cluster over 6 days

cluster_thesis.text: Demand is not the problem: TSMC's August revenue rose 53.3% YoY and 10.1% MoM, and Lam lifted its 2026 WFE view to the low-$150B range. The -3.2% 1m cluster mean and today's pre-open selloff are macro-driven plus a China export-control discount on the front-end toolmakers. Downgraded from strengthening to intact because the extra WFE dollars are being taxed by China controls (AMAT -$600-710M FY26), and that tax falls unevenly inside the cluster.
cluster_thesis.falsifier: TSMC September revenue (about 2026-10-09) below +25% YoY, or a cut to the CoWoS 190-200k wpm end-2027 path on the 2026-10-15 call; separately, ASML Q3 bookings on 2026-10-14 below the prior quarter would mean the front-end recovery has stalled.

margin_pool.moving_toward: The foundry and advanced packaging capacity owner (TSM pricing power, CoWoS), plus test and process control at leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM and packaging
margin_pool.moving_away_from: Broad-line deposition/etch and DUV sold into China, where export controls now cover mature-node and memory tools

evidence.claim: TSMC Aug 2026 revenue NT$514.81B, +53.3% YoY, +10.1% MoM; Jan-Aug +39.3%
AMAT estimates FY26 revenue reduced by $600-710M from US China export restrictions; controls extend to mature-node and memory tools
evidence.source: 247wallst / AlphaSpread coverage of AMAT Q3 call

evidence.claim: Leading-edge foundry logic, DRAM and advanced packaging drive ~80% of WFE growth in 2026-27; Lam sees 2026 WFE in the low-$150B range vs $140B earlier
Test rose from 7% to 8% of semicap spend in 2026
evidence.source: Teradyne Q2 FY26 call (prior ladder, not re-verified)

differentiator_reads.axis: advanced packaging (CoWoS-class) capacity as a distinct bottleneck
differentiator_reads.read: Owns the bottleneck and prices it. August +53.3% YoY puts it well past the +25% falsifier, and price agrees (rel_intra +4.2pp) because revenue is accelerating, not on sentiment.

differentiator_reads.axis: foundry customer concentration and whether the customer gains share
differentiator_reads.read: Its customers (NVDA, AVGO, AMD, QCOM) all run through it, so it captures share gains by any of them.

ranking.case_against: Taiwan geopolitical tail; a ~25% AI-wafer price hike could meet customer pushback; Q3 print 2026-10-15 is the next test, and monthly revenue is lumpy (Sept has been soft in past years).

differentiator_reads.read: Test is the only step with a sourced share gain (7% to 8%). Not re-verified this run.

ranking.case_against: Price has rolled over (rel_intra -2.5pp, was +8.8pp at the 09-08 ladder). The front end is guided to out-grow test in 2027, and test historically lags a WFE turn. cap_multiple 0.92 leaves little room. The open flag calls the position dust, which conflicts with the $1.78k row.

differentiator_reads.read: Process-control dollars per wafer rise with GAA layer count and packaging inspection. Q4 FY26 beat and $7B buyback.
Named alongside AMAT/LRCX in the expanded mature-node/memory restrictions; the move is priced in (rel_intra -10.1pp).

ranking.case_against: Two beat-and-fall reactions in a row; -13.3% 1m; China share not quantified this run. It ranks above price only on process-mix intensity, which is a structural argument, not a dated datapoint.

differentiator_reads.axis: foundry/IDM customer concentration and share gain
differentiator_reads.read: Leads on price (rel_intra +14.8pp) because of new AI-datacenter partnerships (AWS, $5B AI-chip revenue targeted by FY27). That is a target, not booked revenue; its core exposure is still handsets, off this cluster's WFE axes.

ranking.case_against: Price leadership rests on an announcement, not on any capacity or share axis. RSI 66 after +11.6%. The FY27 AI revenue is unproven until the 2026-10-30 print.

differentiator_reads.read: China ~20% of 2026 sales, with the MATCH Act threatening DUV to China; the EUV monopoly is untouched.
A raised 2026 WFE (low-$150B) helps litho with a lag; bookings on 10-14 are the read-through for AMAT/KLAC 2-3 quarters out.

ranking.case_against: (For it) the lowest ATR in the cluster (2.82%) and analyst mean target $2,168. Its rank would jump if Q3 bookings beat, so it may be mispriced low rather than a laggard.

differentiator_reads.read: The only member with a quantified hit: -$600-710M FY26 revenue from the expanded controls covering mature-node and memory tools, a direct hit to its broad-line dep/etch franchise.
differentiator_reads.source: AMAT Q3 FY26 call coverage (247wallst, AlphaSpread)

differentiator_reads.read: Mature-node and China share is higher than at KLAC/ASML-EUV, so it is the most exposed to the mature-node overcapacity plus controls combination.

ranking.case_against: Q3 beat ($9.12B vs $9.0B) with a Q4 guide of $10.25B±0.5B; AMAT says leading-edge, DRAM and packaging drive ~80% of WFE growth; analyst mean target $640.89 vs $456.49 (+40%). After a -16.7% 1m move, much of the China discount may already be priced, which makes it the likeliest name to reorder up.

unranked.reason: A compute designer, not a WFE/process-step participant. Every playbook axis is N/A, so a rank would be price-only (rel_intra +10.1pp). Belongs on a compute/accelerator ladder.

reorder_when: TSMC Sept revenue (~2026-10-09) below +25% YoY: TSM falls below TER/KLAC
ASML Q3 net bookings on 2026-10-14 above Q2 with China below 20% of sales: ASML moves to rank 3 or above
TER Q3 on 2026-10-22 guides Q4 below consensus or cuts its test-share commentary: TER falls below KLAC
AMAT reaffirms or narrows the China hit below $600M by 2026-11-13, or the China control expansion is paused: AMAT leaves the laggard slot
QCOM 2026-10-30 print discloses booked AI-datacenter revenue at or above $500M/qtr: QCOM moves to rank 2 or above

redundant_pairs.same_bet_because: Business screen, not a correlation (the compute screen returned none): both are US front-end semicap names facing the same China controls and the same foundry/memory customers, but at different process steps (dep/etch vs process control)

bench.why_better_than: ASML: a direct OSAT/advanced-packaging exposure to where the margin pool is moving, with no China-DUV policy overhang (analyst mean target $76.40)
bench.entry_condition: Holds above $50 through the macro selloff, and TSMC keeps the CoWoS path on 2026-10-15 (AMKR is the overflow/US packaging partner)

bench.why_better_than: AMAT: etch/dep more tilted to DRAM/HBM and GAA, and management raised 2026 WFE to low-$150B (analyst mean target $370.87). China exposure is similar, so this is a partial substitute, not an escape
bench.entry_condition: ASML bookings on 2026-10-14 confirm front-end orders; avoid if new China controls land before then

catalysts.event: TSMC Q3 call: capex and CoWoS path
Applied Materials Q4 FY26 (China hit update)

thesis_tensions.tension: Ranked last on quantified China export-control revenue loss, while thesis carries strengthening on the Q3 beat and guide. Thesis also describes the position as dust (0.012%), which conflicts with the $1,291 ladder row.
The ladder keeps TER high on test share, but it lost cluster leadership in 6 days. Open flag calls the position dust while the ladder row shows $1,781; one of the two is stale.

prior_ladder_review.why: TER went from +8.8pp to -2.5pp rel_intra within 6 days, and the #2 pick KLAC fell to -10.1pp. INTC was sold, so the laggard call cannot be scored (a sale is consistent with the call). Only the #3 pick, TSM, held up on both price and fundamentals, so it is promoted to leader on dated revenue evidence.
